title: c-parser AST JSON Schema (v1.0)

version.description: AST schema version. Bumped on incompatible changes; `code-bridge` rejects mismatched MAJOR versions.

language.description: Source language identifier. Fixed to "c" for this parser; the field exists for the multi-language `code-bridge` family (cpp-parser, rust-parser, ...).

source_length.description: Length of the original source buffer in bytes. Hard upper bound for every `span.end` (checked by the custom validator).

root.description: Index into `nodes` of the root node. Must reference an existing node (checked by the custom validator).

nodes.description: Flat arena of AST nodes. `root` and every `children[]` entry must reference existing indices into this array.

errors.description: Non-fatal diagnostics collected during lexing/parsing. Fatal errors are surfaced via the API/CLI, not through this array.

Span.description: Half-open byte range [start, end) into the original source buffer. Invariants `start <= end` and `end <= source_length` are checked by the custom validator, not by JSON Schema.

NodeKind.description: Structural kind of the AST node. Naming convention: `kind` and `data.type` usually coincide, but several kinds use a shortened `data.type`: `FunctionDefinition` → `FunctionDef`, `VariableDeclaration` → `VariableDecl`, `ParameterDeclaration` → `ParameterDecl`, `TypedefDeclaration` → `TypedefDecl`, `StructDeclaration` → `StructDef`, `UnionDeclaration` → `UnionDef`, `EnumDeclaration` → `EnumDef`. Kinds without a corresponding `Data*` schema are structural and must carry `data: null` (e.g. `CompoundStatement`, `IfStatement`, `ParenExpr`, `TypeSpecifier`, `NullStatement`).

Node.description: A single AST node. `children` holds structural child indices (empty for leaves). Payload, if any, lives in `data` and MUST be discriminated by its `type` field. Per-kind enforcement of the (kind, data) pairing is implemented via the `allOf` block below.

children.description: Ordered list of child node indices. May be empty.

data.description: Tagged union payload, or `null` for structural kinds without attributes. See the per-kind enforcement in the `allOf` block below.

allOf.description: Per-kind enforcement: exactly one branch must match. Structural kinds require `data: null`; kinds carrying attributes require the corresponding `Data<Kind>` object.

oneOf.description: Structural kinds — no payload, `data` MUST be `null`.

NodeData.description: Tagged union of node payloads. Each branch is a JSON object with a required `type` field acting as the discriminator. Exactly one branch must match. This definition is used for top-level `data` validation; per-kind strictness (kind ↔ data pairing) is additionally enforced in `Node.allOf`.

name.description: Materialized identifier text extracted from the source by Span (lossy UTF-8).

value.description: Numeric literal text as written in the source (may include prefixes and hex digits).

suffix.description: Type suffix as written in the source: "u", "l", "ul", "ll", "ull". `null` and absent are both accepted: absent corresponds to Rust's `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`; `null` corresponds to plain `Option::None` serialization. Consumers must treat absent and `null` identically (no suffix).
Float suffix: "f", "l", "F", "L". `null` and absent are both accepted (see `DataIntegerLiteral.suffix`).

value.description: Raw literal text (with surrounding quotes) as it appears in the source, materialized by Span.

encoding.description: Encoding prefix (C11): "u8", "u", "U", "L". `null` and absent are both accepted (see `DataIntegerLiteral.suffix`).

DataCharLiteral.description: Payload for `NodeKind: CharLiteral`. Character literals in C may carry an encoding prefix: `L'a'`, `u'z'`, `U'Я'`, `u8'x'`. Whether the parser distinguishes them is a parser-side decision; the schema reserves the optional `encoding` field for that purpose and does not require it.

value.description: Raw character literal text (with surrounding single quotes) as it appears in the source, materialized by Span. May include the encoding prefix if the parser chooses to preserve it verbatim (e.g. `L'a'`); consumers MUST NOT rely on either behavior and should consult `encoding` when semantic distinction matters.

encoding.description: Optional encoding prefix (C11): "u8", "u", "U", "L". Absent or `null` means: no prefix, OR the parser does not distinguish prefixes for char literals at the AST level. See the description of `DataCharLiteral`.

is_macro.description: Optional. True if the parser identified the callee as a macro invocation rather than a function call. Absent means "unknown / not distinguished"; consumers must default to `false`. See `DataCallExpr` description for the full contract.

is_variadic.description: true for VLA (variable-length array) sizeof operands such as `sizeof(int[n])`; false for plain `sizeof` applied to a type name or an expression.

DataFunctionDef.description: Payload for `NodeKind: FunctionDefinition`. Note the shortened discriminator `FunctionDef`.

storage_class.description: Storage-class specifier text: "extern", "static", "inline", or "" if absent.

DataVariableDecl.description: Payload for `NodeKind: VariableDeclaration`. Note the shortened discriminator `VariableDecl`.

DataParameterDecl.description: Payload for `NodeKind: ParameterDeclaration`. Note the shortened discriminator `ParameterDecl`.

DataTypedefDecl.description: Payload for `NodeKind: TypedefDeclaration`. Note the shortened discriminator `TypedefDecl`.

DataStructDef.description: Payload for `NodeKind: StructDeclaration`. Note the shortened discriminator `StructDef`.

name.description: Struct tag name, or `null` for an anonymous struct type.

DataUnionDef.description: Payload for `NodeKind: UnionDeclaration`. Note the shortened discriminator `UnionDef`.

DataEnumDef.description: Payload for `NodeKind: EnumDeclaration`. Note the shortened discriminator `EnumDef`.

value.description: Explicit enumerator value as written in the source (materialized string), or `null`/absent if implicit.

DataPreprocessorDirective.description:
Payload for all `NodeKind: Preprocessor*` kinds. `directive` is expected to match the kind suffix (e.g. `PreprocessorInclude` → "include"); this cross-check is enforced by the custom validator, not by JSON Schema.

Contract for `argument`: the field is unconditionally present and is always a JSON string. Directives without arguments (e.g. `#else`, `#endif`) serialize as `"argument": ""` — never as `null` and never omitted. On the Rust side this corresponds to a plain `String` (not `Option<String>`), which is the natural representation for raw, unexpanded directive text.

argument.description: Raw argument text up to end of line (unexpanded). Empty string (`""`) for directives without arguments. MUST NOT be `null` and MUST NOT be omitted; on the Rust side this is `String`, not `Option<String>`.

DataErrorNode.description: Payload for `NodeKind: ErrorNode`. Ensures the AST remains a connected graph and errors can be located via the top-level `errors` array (see ТЗ §5.6).

error_index.description: Index into the top-level `errors` array. Must reference an existing entry (checked by the custom validator).

Error.description: A single lexical, syntactic, or semantic diagnostic.
